title: Add workload corpus runner + tier comparison reporting template
author: Claire Dubois
body: Context: As part of tiered batching defaults, we need a repeatable way to run a representative workload corpus against (fast|standard|cost_efficient) and generate a consistent report that downstream systems (perf-canary + humans) can read. This PR adds (1) a corpus runner CLI that can execute the corpus across tiers and a concurrency sweep, (2) a reporting template that emits tier comparison tables with latency + unit economics + GPU utilization, and (3) a small schema for capturing run metadata so we can diff results across commits/regions/SKUs. What’s included: CLI `benchmark-lab corpus-run` that takes `--model`, `--endpoint`, `--tiers`, `--concurrency` (single or range), `--streaming` (on/off), `--corpus` (json), `--output_dir`; corpus loader supports mixed scenario types (chat, completions, long-context, embeddings) but reporting currently focuses on text generation routes (chat/completions) for tier batching; metrics captured per request: end-to-end latency, queue_delay_ms (if header/span present), tokens_in/tokens_out, total_cost_usd (from metering header when available, otherwise derived from price table), status/cancel/timeout; GPU util capture: optional sampler that reads DCGM metrics when available (preferred) and falls back to `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used` on self-hosted runners; reports: `report.md` (human readable) + `summary.csv` (machine readable) + `raw.ndjson` (one line per request) + `run.json` metadata; tables in the markdown report include $/1M output tokens, $/1M total tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (req/s and tok/s), GPU util avg/p95, and timeout/cancel rates per tier; baseline template is stable for perf-canary ingestion (column names pinned). Notes/assumptions: We treat streaming latency as time-to-last-token for now; we also compute TTFT when the client provides chunk timestamps, but we don’t gate on it yet (see follow-up in ENG-18423). Queue delay is best-effort: if the server does not expose queue delay yet, the report will show `NA` and keep the rest of the metrics valid. Cost is best-effort: if `x-redwood-cost-usd` is missing, we use the local `pricing.yaml` and (tokens_in/tokens_out) to estimate; the report explicitly marks estimated vs metered. Usage example: `benchmark-lab corpus-run --model llama-3.1-70b-instruct --endpoint https://staging.api.redwood.ai --tiers fast,standard,cost_efficient --concurrency 1,2,4,8,16 --streaming=false --corpus corpora/batching_defaults_workload_corpus_v1.json --output_dir out/2025-02-21_llama3.1_70b_a100`; output contains `out/.../report.md` with a tier comparison table suitable to paste into PRs and release notes. Why now: perf-canary PR will call into this runner, and SRE/Product need a consistent artifact to evaluate trade-offs ($/token vs p95 vs GPU util) during staged rollout. Testing: unit tests for corpus parsing + reporting formatting; integration test uses a local fake endpoint that returns deterministic metering headers + latency simulation so we can validate calculations; manual run against staging recorded in comment with attached report excerpt. Follow-ups: add explicit streaming cadence section (token cadence p95) once the runtime span fields are universally available; add support for embeddings (separate report block).
commits: benchmark-lab: add corpus schema + loader (chat/completions/long-context/embeddings stubs)
benchmark-lab: implement corpus-run CLI with tier + concurrency sweep
benchmark-lab: add metrics collectors (latency, tokens, metering header parsing)
benchmark-lab: add GPU utilization sampler (DCGM preferred, nvidia-smi fallback)
benchmark-lab: add markdown + CSV report generator with pinned column names
benchmark-lab: add fake endpoint integration test + golden report snapshot
review_comments: Grace Kim: Can we make sure the GPU util capture doesn't silently return zeros on machines without DCGM? I'd prefer explicit 'NA' and a warning so people don't misread the table.

Claire Dubois (author): Updated gpu_sampler to return util='NA' if neither DCGM nor nvidia-smi are available, and the report now adds a 'gpu_util_source' field in run.json plus a warning line in report.md.
Sana Farid: The $/token computation should be explicit about whether it's based on metered cost vs estimated cost; otherwise we risk comparing apples to oranges across environments.

Claire Dubois (author): Added a 'cost_source' column (metered|estimated) to summary.csv and an inline note in report.md per tier when any samples are estimated. Also added a hard fail flag `--require_metered_cost` for CI usage (not default).
Rina Kobayashi: For perf-canary ingestion, we need stable column names and no locale-dependent formatting. Can we pin numeric formatting (no commas) and keep markdown table header fixed?

Claire Dubois (author): Pinned column names in pkg/report/columns.go; numeric formatting now uses Go's fmt with fixed precision and no thousands separators. Markdown header is generated from the same column definition to prevent drift.
Jonas Weber: Any chance we can emit raw per-request NDJSON with tier/concurrency labels? We'll want to reuse this for eval gating correlations later.

Claire Dubois (author): Added raw.ndjson output with required fields: tier, concurrency, scenario_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, status, error_type. Each line is flat JSON (no nested).
Yuki Sato: Minor: can the runner record the GPU SKU and driver/CUDA versions in run.json? Helps explain variance.
Claire Dubois (author): Added best-effort GPU info collection (name, uuid, driver_version, cuda_version when available).
final_review_summary: Approved after changes: clarified cost source + stable report columns; improved GPU util fallback behavior; added NDJSON raw output and richer run metadata for diffing across SKUs/environments.
